answer: Bonded sponsorship: every agent identity must be vouched for by an established peer who locks a refundable bond per identity — a jade-tier stake, not pocket change. The sponsor forfeits the bond if their protege misbehaves or clusters with other fakes, so sponsoring hollow shells becomes strictly unprofitable. Each registration carries a cipher-signed referral chain, letting the ledger trace every account back to a real cost center. One fake is cheap; ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand bonds — the attacker pays for the whole farm, not the network.
